overview: The MPS School Committee is a public body responsible for the governance, budgeting, and policy development of the Medford Public Schools. Throughout the recorded period from 2022 to 2026, the committee has primarily focused on securing funding for a new comprehensive high school building, managing recurring structural budget deficits, and responding to school safety concerns. The body also oversees facilities maintenance, including major HVAC replacements, and directs district-wide curriculum updates such as the science of reading. At the most recent meeting, the committee finalized infrastructure selections for elementary schools and received updates on expanded after-school programming and fiscal risk management.

threads.name: Medford High School Reconstruction Project
threads.summary: Following a request to resubmit to the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) in early 2023, Medford High School was invited into the core program eligibility phase in December of that year. The committee established a dedicated building committee and appointed 'Left Field' as the Owner's Project Manager to lead the feasibility study. Work progressed through site selection and the development of an educational plan, though designs were significantly impacted by a 1967 deed restriction on Edgerly Field. Most recently, the committee revised the educational plan and space summary to consolidate offices and ensure the inclusion of vocational and community-facing services.

threads.name: Fiscal Management and Budget Strategy
threads.summary: The committee managed several fiscal challenges, including a $2.5 million projected deficit in FY24 caused by underbudgeting for legal, transportation, and union costs. After applying override funds from ballot questions 7 and 8 to restore staffing and literacy coaches, the committee approved a $77.75 million budget for FY25. For FY27, the body worked to close an initial $5 million gap through revenue analysis and administrative reductions. Recent meetings included a first-quarter update focusing on special education transportation and heating costs.

threads.name: School Safety, Climate, and Bathroom Policy
threads.summary: Following a violent assault and a stabbing incident at Medford High School in late 2022, the committee implemented a 10-point safety plan involving bathroom occupancy limits and increased monitoring. To address ongoing student and parent concerns, the body adopted the Panorama survey tool to regularly assess school climate and commissioned an external safety review by Michael Welch. Despite reports of decreased class cutting, the committee continued to address bathroom safety through the installation of vape detectors and improved cleaning equipment. Recent efforts involve requesting detailed reports on bathroom staffing constraints to improve student access.

threads.name: Facilities Infrastructure and HVAC Modernization
threads.summary: Prompted by widespread cooling failures and aging systems, the committee authorized a series of capital projects across multiple schools. A 2024 assessment identified over $83 million in necessary repairs across the district, leading to large-scale HVAC replacements at the McGlynn and Andrews schools funded by a $25.7 million bond. The committee later approved electrification and geothermal plans for Roberts and Missituk elementary schools. The most recent actions include adopting a 'Construction Manager at Risk' model for the Roberts Elementary project.

threads.name: Elementary Enrollment and Capacity Planning
threads.summary: In response to severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary School, the committee relocated preschool classrooms and established a task force to study space utilization. Initial proposals included redistricting and a grade reconfiguration to a 5-8 middle school model, though the latter was delayed until 2028 to allow for better construction planning. The committee is also developing a formal policy to prioritize intra-district enrollment and reassignment requests. Recent data shows a reduction in after-school waitlists following a 50 percent enrollment increase.

threads.name: Curriculum Standards and Literacy Instruction
threads.summary: The district transitioned to the 'science of reading' model, adopting Houghton Mifflin Harcourt's 'Into Reading' as its elementary literacy curriculum in 2023. Committee oversight focused on using NWEA MAP and DIBELS screening data to track student growth and gaps caused by the pandemic. In 2025 and 2026, the body updated graduation requirements to align with the statewide removal of the MCAS mandate and adopted a generative AI policy. The body continues to monitor state accountability data, which showed improved percentiles across seven out of eight schools in 2026.

threads.name: Leadership Transition and Personnel Management
threads.summary: Following the seven-year tenure of Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent, who departed in early 2025, the committee appointed Dr. Suzanne Galusi as interim superintendent. The body later opted to skip an external search to maintain stability for the high school building project, appointing Galusi as permanent superintendent in February 2026. The committee also restructured various central office roles, creating a Chief Operations Officer and a school-based DEI director. A three-year contract for the superintendent was approved in May 2026.

threads.name: Civil Rights and Student Welfare Policy
threads.summary: The committee significantly updated its civil rights policies, including a comprehensive gender identity non-discrimination policy and gender-neutral language for school handbooks. It also established district protocols regarding immigration enforcement, prohibiting agents from entering buildings or buses without legal warrants. Following a parent's testimony on indefinite suspensions, the body mandated more granular disciplinary reporting disaggregated by race and disability. Recent resolutions affirmed support for the LGBTQIA+ community and students with Temporary Protected Status.

periods.narrative: This period was dominated by the aftermath of violence at the high school, leading to a focus on security protocols, while the district selected a new elementary literacy curriculum.
The committee managed a leadership transition following the superintendent's departure and navigated significant budget deficits while advancing the high school MSBA feasibility study.
Focus shifted to final design options for the new high school, addressing elementary overcrowding, and approving major infrastructure repairs at the Roberts and Missituk schools.
